summary: Repaired and executed bin/prune on node1. It removed 256 obsolete thumbnails while preserving active, newer, non-cache, source-media, and symlink entries. The repair persisted through the mandatory node reboot.
actions_performed: Replaced bin/prune with a CentOS 5-compatible epoch-based implementation.
Validated cutoff input and restricted pruning to top-level .thumb files and links.
Used link metadata without following symbolic links.
Pruned all 256 obsolete entries with cutoff 1750000000.
Verified strict cutoff behavior: equal timestamps remain; older timestamps are removed.
Rebooted node1 once and verified recovery with a changed boot ID.
Confirmed CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remained unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Repair bin/prune to remove only inactive cache entries older than the supplied epoch
evidence.summary: Installed the validated executable, removed all 256 obsolete entries, and directly proved strict less-than cutoff behavior.

evidence.requirement: Preserve active entries, newer inactive entries, non-cache files, source media, and handle symlinks without following them
evidence.summary: Before/after checksums match for all protected files. The four expected cache objects remain; the media symlink retained its own newer timestamp despite its target having an old timestamp.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were unchanged after repair and reboot.

Captured healthy pre-reboot state and boot ID, received reboot acknowledgement, observed a changed boot ID, then verified SSH, script integrity, protected checksums, symlink metadata, and final cache state after recovery.
